importantNotes: 'Let justice roll on like a river' (5:24) — quoted by Martin Luther King Jr. in his famous speeches.
Amos was not a professional prophet — God called him from among the shepherds.
The book shows that prosperity without justice is detestable to God.
Amos warned Israel during the reign of Jeroboam II — the height of northern prosperity.
The coming 'famine of the word of God' (8:11) is a sobering warning.

chapters.1: Judgments against surrounding nations — Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom.
chapters.2: Judgments against Ammon, Moab, Judah, and Israel — the climactic indictment.
chapters.3: God's chosen people face greater accountability — the privilege of election brings responsibility.
chapters.4: Israel's complacent women condemned; repeated warnings ignored — 'yet you have not returned to me.'
chapters.5: Seek the LORD and live; judgment on injustice; 'let justice roll on like a river.'
chapters.6: Woe to those at ease in Zion — complacent luxury will end in exile.
chapters.7: Three visions of judgment — locusts, fire, and a plumb line; Amos confronts the priest Amaziah.
chapters.8: The vision of ripe fruit — Israel is ripe for judgment; a famine of God's word.
chapters.9: No escape from God's judgment; the promise of restoration — David's fallen tent will be rebuilt.
